Tests {@link CodecEncoding}, the helper that maps between Pack200 meta-encoding specifier bytes and the {@link Codec} instances they describe.
The specifier value 116 introduces an "arbitrary" (non-canonical) BHSD codec whose B/H/S/D parameters are read from the accompanying header bytes.

Specifier values in (116, 141) denote run codecs, and values in (140, 189) denote population codecs. The tests assert the leading specifier byte falls in the matching range without pinning the exact value.

Reconstructs the codec described by a specifier array: the leading element is the specifier value and the remaining elements are the header bytes consumed while decoding. This is the inverse of {@link CodecEncoding#getSpecifier}.
Asserts the three defining fields of a RunCodec round-trip unchanged.
These are the canonical encodings specified by the Pack200 spec
A canonical codec's specifier is just its index, with no trailing header bytes.
Specifier value 0 means "use the supplied default codec".
Simple run codec round-trips through its specifier.
One codec is the same as the default
Nested with one the same as the default
